tagline: Down the Rogue River canyon on a narrow paved road.
intro: From the Merlin exit on I-5 the Merlin-Galice Road heads west through Merlin to the Rogue, then follows the deep river canyon, rock walls bordered by forested slopes, past Hellgate Canyon to Galice. There are pullouts and numerous river access points. For one stretch the byway climbs away from the river into the Siskiyou Mountains, among stands of Douglas fir.

Galice was settled in 1852 as a mining camp on Galice Creek, went over to logging in the 20th century and then to the tourist trade. Hellgate Canyon, close by, was a filming location for John Wayne's Rooster Cogburn in 1975.

moments.title: Merlin
moments.text: The railroad station here opened in 1883 as Jump Off Joe, after a local stream, and in 1886 a railroad engineer renamed it for the merlins he saw in the area.

moments.title: Galice
moments.text: The town began as Galiceburg up Galice Creek, a hot spot for gold prospectors in the 1850s, and now sits on the Rogue itself, just downstream from the creek's mouth.

moments.title: Rand Ranger Station
moments.text: Now the Smullin Visitor Center, 18 miles in. The first ranger lived here in a tent for eight years, until the mining company owning it rented the Forest Service a parcel at $1 yearly.

practical: The byway is paved and open year round but narrow and winding, with single-lane stretches and occasional turnouts, and roads beyond it are often closed by snow in winter.

sources.label: FHWA, Galice to Hellgate Back Country Byway
